children: Shares of Indoco Remedies Ltd. fell as much as 5.5% on Monday, September 7, after the US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) issued seven observations to the company following an inspection of its manufacturing facility in Goa.
The USFDA inspected the company's Plant II (Sterile) facility in Goa from August 27 to September 4, 2026. At the conclusion of the inspection, the company received seven observations in Form 483.
Indoco Remedies said it is addressing the observations comprehensively and will submit its response to the USFDA within the stipulated timeframe.

Form 483 observations are issued by the USFDA when its investigators identify conditions that may constitute violations of regulatory requirements during an inspection. The observations do not represent a final regulatory determination.

Indoco Remedies reported an improvement in its June quarter performance, returning to a net profit of ₹65 crore, compared to a net loss of ₹36 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue from operations rose 6.4% year-on-year to ₹467 crore from ₹439 crore in Q1FY26.

Operating performance also improved, with Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) rising to ₹40.8 crore from ₹16.7 crore a year earlier. EBITDA margin expanded to 8.7% from 3.8% in the corresponding quarter last year.

After falling as much as 5.5% to an intraday low of ₹248.06 on Monday, shares of Indoco Remedies are now trading 3.1% lower at ₹254.49. The stock has risen 15% over the last one month, thereby turning positive on a year-to-date basis as well.

title: Indoco Remedies shares fall nearly 6% after USFDA flags seven observations at Goa plant
